subject: Strategic renewal: phased uplift + on-demand cushion
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Ramos <ellie.ramos@novacorp.com>, Novacorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Strategic renewal: phased uplift + on-demand cushion

Hi Ellie / procurement team —

Thanks again for the productive renewal discussion last week. Attached is a clean SOW (Novacorp_SOW_v3.pdf) and a short export of your usage (usage_history_Q1-Q2.csv) so you have the numbers behind our proposal.

High-level proposal (for discussion):
- 12-month renewal with a phased committed uplift: 0–3 months = +20% baseline commit, 4–6 months = +40% baseline commit, remainder = committed level holds.
- 3-month price hold on the currently-negotiated unit rate for the initial phase to give you runway while integrating new features.
- On-demand cushion: a shared burst pool (pay-as-you-go at a capped rate) to handle spikes—no instant overage at list price.
- Ramp credits: one-time credit applied at month 4 if usage exceeds committed uplift by >25% to smooth shortfall reconciliation.

Questions for you: procurement timeline for an amendment, whether legal needs a tracked SOW redline, and whether Novacorp wants the cushion as a pre-purchased burst or pay-as-you-go with a capped surcharge.

Next steps I suggest: quick 30-min call Wed to align, then we can route a draft amendment to Legal and Finance.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Novacorp_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW, redline-ready), usage_history_Q1-Q2.csv (token & embedding breakdown)

From: Ellie Ramos <ellie.ramos@novacorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Novacorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 13:45:12 -0000
Subject: Re: Strategic renewal: phased uplift + on-demand cushion

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear options and the files. A couple of constraints from procurement / finance:
1) We need a guaranteed price hold for at least 6 months on the committed unit rate — otherwise we get pushed into an internal approval loop.
2) The initial commit increase needs to be lower (finance prefers a 10–15% step at go-live), with a pre-defined ramp schedule tied to usage thresholds.
3) For the cushion, procurement prefers a prepaid burst pool (one-time commitment against a discounted burst rate) rather than a per-call surcharge — simpler for our cost forecasting.

Can you share a version of the SOW that reflects: 6-month price hold OR a compromise (3 months price hold + written cap on allowed list-price increases)? Also can you outline the credit mechanics (how the ramp credit triggers and how it's applied to invoices)?

If we can get a short amendment draft and a clear table that shows monthly commit vs. expected billing, we can fast-track to legal.

Thanks —
Ellie Ramos
Director, AI Platforms 
Novacorp

[Sent from mobile]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellie Ramos <ellie.ramos@novacorp.com>, Novacorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:02:35 -0000
Subject: Re: Strategic renewal: phased uplift + on-demand cushion

Karthik / team —

Adding a few pragmatic options from pricing that tend to land well with procurement:

Option A (procurement-friendly):
- Initial commit uplift: +12% months 0–3, +28% months 4–6, then +40% thereafter.
- 6-month price hold on core unit rate.
- Prepaid burst pool: 25% of month-6 expected usage purchased at a 20% discount vs list for cushion.
- Ramp credit: if usage exceeds month-6 expected by >20%, apply a prorated credit equal to 50% of the overage surcharge (applied to the following invoice).

Option B (lower cash outlay for customer):
- Initial commit uplift: +8% month 0–3, +20% month 4–6.
- 3-month price hold + guaranteed cap on rate increases (no more than +5% in months 4–6).
- Pay-as-you-go cushion with capped surcharge (cap = 1.5x list rate) and a quarterly reconciliation credit if sustained usage spikes occur.

Operational notes: Legal will want clean language for the credit trigger (clear metric: 7-day rolling avg above committed baseline) and billing (credit applied to next invoice, not retroactive). Finance to confirm whether the ramp credit can be recognized as a one-time contra revenue item.

I can produce a one-page comparison table for Novacorp and draft amendment language for Option A if we want to prioritize procurement's preference.

Happy to hop on a call with Ellie Wed 11:00–11:30 PT if that works.

—Marissa
Sr. Director, Pricing & Renewals
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: sample_credit_table.xlsx (will circulate if we pick an option)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ellie Ramos <ellie.ramos@novacorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Strategic renewal: phased uplift + on-demand cushion

Ellie / team —

Thanks for the input — this is helpful. Quick summary and proposed next steps so we have an agreed record before legal: 

1) We will prioritize Option A (procurement-friendly) as Marissa outlined: 6-month price hold, modest initial uplift, and a prepaid burst pool at a 20% discount.
2) Ramp credit mechanics: trigger = sustained 7-day rolling average >20% above committed baseline at month 6; credit = 50% of overage surcharge applied to next invoice. Finance: please confirm contra-revenue treatment.
3) Action owners: 
   - Legal (LAUREN): draft an amendment incorporating Option A language & SOW redlines (LAUREN to push back on indemnities if needed).
   - Pricing (MARRIS A): finalize the credit table and the prepaid burst sizing (Marissa to attach sample_credit_table.xlsx).
   - Sales (KARTHIK): coordinate signatures and follow up with DocuSign link.

Ellie — can you confirm procurement's acceptance of Option A in principle? If yes I'll kick off the amendment draft and loop Legal. If you want to take Option B instead we'll switch to that language (but B will take slightly longer to finalize).

Available for a 30-min call Wed 11:00 PT to lock in details.

Best —
Karthik
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
